parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, facility restriction, or documented police/social hostility toward trans visitors; foreign documents are accepted, and governing-state gender-recognition certificates are recognised in acquired gender. Documented social acceptance is strong (90%+ public support for marriage equality in a ~3,000-person territory) and marriage/civil-partnership access is open on equal terms. Negative and open items: no gender-identity ground in the constitution, hate-stirring or aggravated-sentencing ordinances (thin formal recourse if bias occurs); no self-ID or non-binary recognition; prisons ordinance content undocumented; no data on trans-specific violence, police practice, or custody placement. Per the rubric, these are open questions and resident gaps, lighter than any documented exposure. But under rule 3 and rule 13, a small jurisdiction with no documented protective enforcement and unanswered custody/violence questions sits a step below the acceptance-with-protections tier (0.85): thin data in a small place cannot be read as proof of safety, though nothing documented is adverse. Reduced-risk band, mid-to-upper: 0.74.
